challenges.title: Sum of Two Numbers
challenges.details: Implement `solve(int a, int b)` and return the sum of the two inputs.

aiTestConfig.promptTemplate:
You are a Java coding challenge assistant. Generate {count} additional test cases for the method `{methodContract}`. The method should return the sum of its two integer arguments. Edge cases to explore: integer overflow boundaries, very large negatives, mixing zero with positives or negatives.

Existing examples for reference:
{examples}

Respond ONLY with a JSON array. Each element must have: "name" (string), "input" ([int, int]), "expected" (int).

hints: The `+` operator on two ints gives the sum.

challenges.title: Concurrent Graph BFS Queries
challenges.details: Implement `solve(int[][] edges, int start, int target)` and return the shortest hop count in an undirected graph. Return `-1` when no path exists.
challenges.methodContract: int solve(int[][] edges, int start, int target)
challenges.explanation: Use BFS and careful state handling.

aiTestConfig.promptTemplate:
You are a Java coding challenge assistant. Generate {count} additional test cases for `{methodContract}`. The method finds the shortest hop count (BFS) between `start` and `target` in an undirected graph represented as an edge list. Return -1 if unreachable.

Explore: cyclic graphs, self-loops, single-node graphs, highly connected graphs, long linear chains.

Existing examples:
{examples}

Respond ONLY with a JSON array. Each element: "name" (string), "input" ([int[][], int, int]), "expected" (int).

hints: Use a queue and visited set.

challenges.title: Token Bucket Rate Limiter
challenges.details: Implement a thread-safe token bucket rate limiter. Your `Solution` class must have a constructor `Solution(int capacity, int refillPerSecond)` and a method `boolean acquire()` that returns `true` if a token was available and consumed, or `false` if the bucket is empty. The bucket refills at `refillPerSecond` tokens every second. The limiter must be safe for concurrent access from multiple threads.
challenges.explanation: Use a token bucket algorithm with a capacity ceiling and time-based refill. Protect shared state with locks or atomic operations.

testCases.name: no tokens rejected when capacity large enough
no data races under high concurrency

aiTestConfig.promptTemplate:
You are a Java coding challenge assistant. Generate {count} additional concurrent test cases for a thread-safe token bucket rate limiter with constructor `Solution(int capacity, int refillPerSecond)` and method `{methodContract}`.

Each test case must include: concurrentThreads, callsPerThread, constructorArgs ([capacity, refillPerSecond]), and expected thresholds (minAccepted, maxAccepted, maxRejected, expectNoExceptions).

Explore: single-thread correctness, many threads few tokens, capacity=0, rapid repeated calls, burst then drain.

Existing examples:
{examples}

Respond ONLY with a JSON array. Each element: "name" (string), "concurrentThreads" (int), "callsPerThread" (int), "constructorArgs" ([int, int]), "expected" ({minAccepted, maxAccepted, maxRejected, expectNoExceptions}).

hints: What shared state does a token bucket need? (current tokens, last refill timestamp)
How do you prevent two threads from consuming the same token? Think `synchronized` or `AtomicInteger`.
Refill logic: calculate elapsed time since last acquire, add (elapsed * refillPerSecond) tokens, cap at capacity.
examples: capacity=10, 20 threads call acquire() once each -> 10 accepted, 10 rejected
capacity=10, 5 threads call acquire() once each -> 5 accepted, 0 rejected
capacity=5, refill=0, 1 thread calls 15 times -> 5 accepted, 10 rejected
challenges.notes: This challenge tests thread safety. A correct but non-thread-safe implementation will fail the high-concurrency test.

challenges.title: User Table CRUD with JDBC
challenges.details: You are given a live `java.sql.Connection` backed by an in-memory H2 database. The `users` table has already been created with columns `id INTEGER`, `name VARCHAR`, `email VARCHAR`, `active BOOLEAN`. Write Java code using JDBC inside `solve(Connection conn)` to: (1) insert three users (Alice active, Bob active, Charlie inactive), (2) update Alice's email from `alice@example.com` to `alice@company.com`, and (3) delete all inactive users. The harness calls `solve(conn)`, then runs verification queries to assert the final state of the table.
challenges.explanation: Use `conn.createStatement()` and `stmt.execute(String sql)` — or `PreparedStatement` for bonus points. The connection and schema are managed by the harness; you only write the DML logic.

testCases.name: exactly two users remain after delete
testCases.description: The harness calls solve(conn), then asserts the total row count. Charlie (inactive) must have been deleted, leaving Alice and Bob.

testCases.name: Alice's email is updated
testCases.description: The harness asserts the email column for Alice after solve(conn) returns.
testCases.assertQuery: SELECT email FROM users WHERE name = 'Alice'

testCases.name: no inactive users remain
testCases.description: All rows with active=FALSE must have been removed by the user's Java JDBC delete statement.
testCases.assertQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE active = FALSE

testCases.name: active users have correct names and emails
testCases.description: The harness runs an ORDER BY query after solve(conn) and compares all columns row-by-row.
testCases.assertQuery: SELECT name, email FROM users WHERE active = TRUE ORDER BY name

sandboxProfile.setup: CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, email VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL, active BOOLEAN NOT NULL);

aiTestConfig.promptTemplate:
You are a Java coding challenge assistant. The user writes a Java method `void solve(Connection conn) throws SQLException` that performs JDBC INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE against a `users` table (columns: id INTEGER, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR, active BOOLEAN).

The harness calls solve(conn), then runs SQL assertions against the resulting table state. Generate {count} additional assertion test cases that verify aspects of the final table state the existing tests do not cover.

Each test case describes WHAT THE HARNESS ASSERTS after the user's Java code runs — not what the user writes. Focus on: individual column values, combined WHERE conditions, ordering, edge cases like Bob's unchanged email.

Existing assertions for context:
{examples}

Respond ONLY with a JSON array. Each element must have: "name" (string), "description" (string explaining what Java scenario this validates), "assertQuery" (SQL the harness runs), and either "expectedSingleValue" (int or string) or "expectedRows" (array of column->value objects).

hints: Your INSERT statements need four values: id, name, email, active. Use TRUE/FALSE for the boolean.
The UPDATE must target Alice specifically — use a WHERE clause on name or id.
DELETE WHERE active = FALSE will remove all users who are not active.
examples: After solve(): users table has 2 rows (Alice active, Bob active)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE active = FALSE -> 0
challenges.notes: The table schema is created for you by the test harness before your code runs. Do not CREATE TABLE — just INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
